purpose: Make the database-versus-cognitive-simulation boundary deterministic enough that variable-N modules can restart, rejoin, resize, and delegate to Claude Code without turning model/workspace state into a second truth store.

placement_rules.when: value carries canonical fact/evidence identity, capability/security authority, effect outcome/journal identity, or exact causal/generation/epoch identity
value must survive module restart/grid resize and loss would change the accepted task/project/evidence state
value is an exact counter/id/digest/checkpoint/configuration or long-lived goal that should not be regenerated probabilistically
value is shared cognitive coordination state whose loss may reduce efficiency but can be deterministically reconstructed without changing canonical history
value is a hypothesis, plan, route, summary, uncertainty estimate, salience score, or workspace winner before deterministic admission
value is local model state, hidden activation, scratchpad, simulation branch, or temporary alternative not required by another module
classification is ambiguous between S0 and a noncanonical class and loss could alter truth/effect/security semantics
classification is ambiguous but the value is clearly nonauthoritative and safely reproducible

decision_questions: Would losing this value across restart/grid resize change canonical accepted history or authority?
Must two modules agree byte-for-byte rather than approximately?
Is the value an identity, epoch, digest, checkpoint, provenance, capability, effect, durable memory, long-lived goal, or exact configuration?
Can the value be deterministically rebuilt from S0 without changing semantics?
Is the value speculative/model-generated/workspace-derived rather than admitted fact?
Is it model/runtime-specific internal state whose persistence would falsely imply cross-model meaning?
Could storing it as canonical cause majority/recurrence/model confidence to become truth?
Does the value need to be queryable/auditable long after the cognitive episode ends?
variable_grid_invariants: S0 semantics do not depend on module count N
module identity is not cognitive-process identity
restart or replacement may discard S2 and rebuild S1 from S0 without changing canonical history
grid resize cannot grant new capabilities or effect authority
coordinator election or workspace majority cannot promote S1 into S0
the same admitted executor may perform different cognitive process types when route and capability bindings permit

first_executable_discriminator.name: RESTART_RESIZE_DB_BOUNDARY_SMOKE
steps: seed S0 with one admitted task identity, generation, durable goal, evidence ref and exact epoch/digest
derive S1 work/workspace projections and create S2 local hypotheses on one module
emit one DbWriteProposal for a permitted durable memory update but do not mutate S0 directly
restart the module, discard S2, and rebuild required S1 from S0 plus admitted transition receipts
change grid size N and route a different cognitive process to the restarted executor without changing S0 semantic identity
attempt direct model-to-S0, stale-generation write, S1-cache-as-recovery-authority and direct-effect variants and require rejection
bridge one bounded request/result through ClaudeCodeBridgePacket and require candidate/evidence-bound reentry rather than direct S0 mutation
first_executable_discriminator.pass: canonical S0 identity remains stable across restart and N change; required S1 rebuilds; S2 loss is tolerated; admitted durable proposal path succeeds; all four authority violations reject

counterhypotheses: Persisting more workspace state may appear more reliable but can create stale second-authority recovery semantics.
Keeping more state ephemeral may appear simpler but can make restart/grid resize silently change accepted history.
A single strong-model transcript may appear sufficient as memory but is not an exact durable state/evidence substrate.
Activation/vector persistence may be useful for research replay but does not make the stored vector a canonical fact.
